C：模拟，设置状态变量和开始变量，每次关闭后更新下一次开始时间。下一次路过时查看: C: simulation. Keep a state variable and a start-time variable. After each closure, update the next start time. On the next visit, check the state and start time to see whether the state changes. The trap is checking whether any T remains at the end. It tests implementation and reading the statement carefully. If the last sample fails, a hand simulation will show why.

直接贪心就好了，不用担心有没有办法取到这个贪心的，他后面又可以递增又可以递减涵盖: A greedy approach is enough. There's no need to worry about whether the chosen elements can actually form the split: the remaining elements can increase or decrease, so all cases are covered.
第一个数是必须要取的因为子数组考虑原数组顺序，如果第一个数是最小的三个数之一，直: The first element has to be included because the subarrays preserve the original order. If it's one of the three smallest elements, just add those three.
如果不是，那就取第一个和最小的和第二小的。: Otherwise, take the first element and the two smallest remaining elements.
很简单的模拟，但是直接模感觉很搞笑，判定为shit: Very simple simulation, but doing it directly feels silly. Verdict: a shit problem.
这道题目是昨天的进阶版，非常有意思，昨天的错误思路在这道题正好用上了，我觉得我的: This is a harder version of yesterday's problem, and it's interesting. The approach that was wrong yesterday works perfectly here. I think my solution is quite neat, and the code is very simple.
我的思路：每一个递减序列都有可能是答案，通过找到递减序列然后扩展序列找到最优解，: My approach: every decreasing run could be part of the answer. Find each decreasing run, then extend it to find the optimum. The extension doesn't need DP; just keep track of the best interval sum, since we can't skip elements inside an interval.
一开始做个人博客只是为了找工作，写写题解展示项目什么的。不知道哪天的时候，觉得用: I originally started this blog to help with job hunting: write up solutions, show some projects, that sort of thing. At some point I thought it might be nice to keep a diary here too. I enjoy reading other people's blogs. Maybe nobody will ever find mine, but writing makes me happy. Whenever my feelings get tangled up with nowhere to go, I come back to working on this site. I messed up an exam, and yesterday I stayed up until 2 a.m. finishing this.
做项目做到下午6点，一边听着视频的声音一边就在床上不省人事。再次醒来就是晚上9点: I worked on a project until six, then passed out on my bed with a video playing. When I woke up, it was nine. I was lying there without dinner, my stomach growling, thinking that if I keep this up I'll die young. 最近收到了一个面试offer，不知道真假不过还是想尽力准备一下。想思考要不要报一: I recently got an interview invitation. Not sure whether it's legit, but I still want to prepare properly. I'm considering interview coaching. Intangible things really do seem to make more money than practical ones. It feels like a student walking up to a market stall: the moment you arrive, the seller is already calculating how much they can take you for.
这个事情还没给我爸妈商量就出成绩了。考砸的那门课我有所预感，但没想到这么凄惨吧。: Before I could talk to my parents about it, my exam results came out. I had a bad feeling about that one module, but I didn't expect it to be this awful. Before the exam I had AI read previous papers and generate a bunch of practice papers. Then I opened the actual exam and thought: what on earth is any of this? I couldn't even understand half the questions, but I forced myself through them. It was supposed to be an easy module. The lectures were incredibly dull and barely related to computer science. I thought surely it couldn't go that badly. Crying. It's frustrating.
来国外读大学是一个非常匆忙的决定，国内的录取通知书和这边的通知书同一个时间到。年: Studying abroad was a rushed decision. My offer here and my offer back home arrived at the same time. Young and arrogant, I felt different, irreplaceable. For all sorts of reasons, I ended up here. There's always someone better, another world beyond the one you know. Every room holds a different story. You can't even envy people who are clever and also have endless time and energy to work hard. Some people aren't lucky, and don't hide their desires or darker sides either. They get back what they put in. They share what they've gained through talent and effort. Information is real wealth. I'm kidding—where would you find a saint? But even if it's just how things look, that's enough.
我思考着未来，甚至不知道明天吃什么。躲在被窝里玩手机，我知道我该干嘛吗？或许知道: I think about the future without even knowing what I'll eat tomorrow. Hiding under the duvet with my phone, do I know what I'm supposed to do? Maybe. Maybe not. In 2023, 'the future' was my word of the year on NetEase Cloud Music. Now I don't even use it. I'm a rat in the gutter. Someone with only a one-percent chance hopes for that one percent; someone who's only one percent short fears it. Big things and small things twist together like yarn, blocking the tiny opening.
我是个懦夫，用ai掩饰自己的懒惰和愚昧。还是个死宅，体重超标，平时也很少打理自己: I'm a coward, using AI to disguise my laziness and ignorance. A shut-in too, overweight and rarely taking care of myself. Nobody pays attention to how I'm doing. I don't look at myself in the mirror either. I envy people with courage and persistence: losing the weight, running despite their shackles, acting on their ideas. Can I become someone like that? I think. I think so. I want to. Not so that you see me that way, but because that's who I am.
